reason: The hypothesis makes specific mechanistic claims about selective oxidation, reduced diffusivities, and resulting scale properties in HEAs, but cites no prior evidence to support any of these premises. Standard textbook knowledge does not cover the claimed multicomponent diffusion effects in these novel alloys, so the lack of citations leaves all key premises unsupported.
premises: Multiple oxide-forming elements enable selective oxidation in HEAs
Multicomponent chemistry reduces ionic and oxygen diffusivities through the oxide layer
Reduced diffusivities limit further oxidation and favor a dense, adherent barrier
HEA with full set of oxide-formers will form thinner, more continuous, less porous scale than control
Improved scale adhesion results from the multicomponent effect on oxide growth
